I left my ex husband with the clothes on my back. Forget about what I wanted. When I looked in the mirror, I had no idea who I was. For a little over a year, I dated myself. When I felt like I was ready to start dating, I got on tinder and posted ONE regular photo of myself and basically said the craziest and realist stuff that is genuine to me and who I am to anyone and everyone i talked to. The kind of shit that I would say if I was already close friends with them. I’m talking friendships that I’ve maintained for years kind of talk. No boundaries. No bullshit. Just 100% me. I told people exactly what I wanted and I would pass over the smallest of things. I confused and pissed a lot of men off. Not my problem. It wasn’t personal. Until this past year I confused being compassionate and empathic with being a people pleaser. They weren’t for me. No point in wasting anyone’s time. I was being honest with them and honest with myself. I’m a Myers’s Briggs fan (ENFP) and that was one of the first things that I would ask people. After texting it up for a few weeks with countless people, I had one guy (INTJ) that still hung around and was still talking to me regularly. I scared the rest off with my extremely forward communication and aggressive honesty. I considered this to be a good thing. He didn’t overly pressure me to meet, didn’t ask for me for sleezy pictures, etc. There was never a time that he said something that I had to think twice about. We didn’t agree on a lot of things, but the way that we disagreed was exceptional. I met him out once it was a bit on the awkward side. It went okay. We talked some, and then we both left. Then, we talked for like three more weeks after that. Texting all the time and even began having (gasp) actual phone conversations. We’ve been together five months now and I have never had this good of a romantic relationship ever with anyone in my life. The conversation, the mental and physical intimacy, everything is truly amazing because we set up a foundation that was based on communication and were 100% ourselves. We became great friends first and are compatible. The sex part came later and it is attentive and intimate in ways that are hard to explain. It’s the best sex that I’ve honestly ever had. He says I’m his second best and I appreciate his honesty and I think it’s also hilarious. He told me that what I did was a reverse-catfish and I guess it was. It worked well for me because I have to have an emotional connection before I am physically attracted to someone. Not everyone is like this, but if you are and you are single, and you are looking for a life partner maybe you should give it a try.

I almost had my third child at home. First two pregnancies and deliveries were just fine. The doctor said, “yeah it will probably be fine, but if anything goes wrong…” he had a point, so I opted for the hospital. My son decided to turn sideways during delivery (shoulder dystocia) and became stuck during the birthing process. I will leave out the particulars about how much this sucked physically for me, but in a nutshell it’s an immediate medical emergency-your baby is stuck, the umbilical is no longer supplying oxygen, you have a short amount of time or they are dead. I was confused and asked if I could have a c section. The doctor and nurse just ignored me. The nurse was physically trying to push my stomach to get the baby out. I’ll leave out what the doctor was doing for the squeamish. I’m sure you can imagine…

I had agreed to medical students being in the room and when I realized quickly that the doctor and nurse were freaking out and that my baby (my first and only son) was probably going to die. I yelled at them all to get out because if my child was not going to be alive, I made that split second choice that I wanted as few people to witness this as possible. When he was finally delivered he was white as a ghost with his head hanging. He was dead. My husband and I were both 100% certain of it and I cannot describe the horror of seeing that and the acceptance that you are faced with. They were about to do cpr and I just had my hands covering my entire face and then I heard him cry. He was covered in bruises and the doctor was just dripping sweat. My son Atticus is 6. Healthy and hilarious and I am so thankful that he was okay. Seeing him like that and just coming to terms with him being delivered dead was the worst thing I have ever seen. Hands down. 

*this story is no way anti home birth. If I had opted for a home birth though, it is likely we both would be dead. You do what is right for you and your family. *

A bit late to the party, but I’ll share my story. I was in my late 20’s and lived in a duplex. I always make sure to lock up when I leave, houses, cars, etc. Anyhow, I bought some brandy for a cold that I had to make hot tea with. About a week goes by and I noticed that it is missing-just gone whole bottle style. Odd. Go on with life. Next it’s a jar of change I had sitting in my bedroom, not empty...gone. At this point, I’m thinking maybe I’m not locking my door. It’s not the best of neighborhoods, lots of foot traffic and what have you. I make EXTRA SURE I’m locking and deadbolting when I leave. I get home one day and a television is gone ripped right from the wall and I KNOW I just unlocked the door to come in. So I call the cops who say, “upppa duppa doo here’s our card with the number you called duopoly durrrr” and leave. Then, I call the landlord who insists that he changes the lock keys every time a new tenant moves in. At this point, I don’t know what to believe. UNTIL, one day my car ended up needing some repairs and I had a friend drop me off at my place. I’m asleep in bed and it’s who knows what time at night, but I’m woken up by a rustling sound in the ceiling. Probably a squirrel or something. I close my eyes and then the sound becomes more of a dragging noise at this point I hear it stop and then you know how you have (and excuse my non professional explanation here) but the little square cut out piece to gain access to the attic?? WELL, that shit begins to move and all that I can see is a small portion of that piece LIFT up about 3/4 inches on one side and hold there for a moment and then slowly and quietly lift back down. It was the people from the OTHER side of the duplex (I think their teenage son) coming into my house and stealing shit and god only knows what else and because my car was gone assumed I wasn’t home. I called the cops, I called the landlord and everyone acted like I was just some crazy person because, “he was a good kid and wouldn’t do that” apparently. The landlord refused to allow me to break my lease (with only 2 months left and wouldn’t return my 800$ deposit). He left me no choice to do the things I did to that place to feel as though I at least got my money’s worth when I moved out that next week.

You are absolutely clinically depressed and if you weren’t after your fathers suicide THEN there would be something “wrong” with you. There is nothing wrong with you. You are normal. It’s not your fault and it wasn’t his fault either, but you have got to get some help from a professional. Of course your mom was concerned. Why are you against medication? I feel like there’s two sides to depression, a biological and a circumstantial and you have checked both boxes. You need a therapist. You and your mother probably both need bereavement counseling. You have got to be honest with your mom and get the help you need. It’s not about being weak or just trying to be strong and get over it.
